label: x echoed back as the 1st or 2nd copy-phase input
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the input token is x at recall_idx 1 or 2. That means the model just fed back original token 0 = x (step L+1) or original token 1 = x (step L+2). Magnitude depends strongly on position. Echoing the first token x right after <DEL> gives activations of about 0.8-1.0 of max, holds about 81% of the mass, and has 100% precision. Echoing x as the second token gives weak activations (about 0.1-0.4 of max), and these are weakest in short sequences (L=3-4, where some predicted cases are inactive). It does not fire on x in the original phase, on x echoed at recall_idx >= 3, or on any other token (88 stray steps out of 32k, carrying ~0% of mass). Dev F1 0.98, mass recall 1.00.

issues: The false positives are not random. Nearly all of the 1114 test FPs are x at recall_idx 2 in short sequences. At L==3 the predicate fires 441 times but only 5% of those are active (precision 0.05). At L==4 precision is 0.72. At L>=5 precision is 0.9999. The explanation says 'some short-sequence cases in this group are inactive', which undersells L=3: there the second-position echo is almost never active. This is a small effect overall (F1 0.982 -> 0.988 once fixed).
Missed activations: 67 test steps holding 0.0% of mass. They are scattered and tiny (0.01-0.05 of max): x as the 3rd echo, or other tokens at recall_idx 1. This is noise.

The other claims check out. All mass is in the copy phase. recall_idx 1 alone gives precision 1.0 and mass 0.807. recall_idx 2 gives mass 0.193 with a similar active count, so its mean is about 0.24x that of recall_idx 1, consistent with the stated 0.1-0.4 vs 0.8-1.0. There is no activation in the original phase, and recall_idx >= 3 has only 49 dev actives.
